about.text: A fermented milk of the Turkic countries and Bulgaria, a more solid yoghurt than ayran, made from boiled milk left warm for 6-10 hours.

sources.text: The first paragraph of its article, shortened.
The photograph, its author and its licence, from its page.

facts.v: Milk often boiled and reduced by about a third, then fermented 6–10 hours at 20–40 °C without stirring; the whey is drained off for suzma
A thick drinking yoghurt like kefir, served at breakfast and used as a condiment on börek and manty in place of sour cream

sources.text: The names from these, and the making in Russia and the use of gatyk in Turkmenistan from these.
